metadata:

name: exp2-iter1-open-ended-range
description: Exp2 iter-1 cand_5 — 10 participants in 2 cell groups (exp1 cells + new); edge/fuzzy/endpoint screens null; open-ended range discount +1.6 nats submitted
metadata:
  type: project
---
Exp2 iter 1, candidate_5 (2026-10-30). This was a refinement slot built on `relative_width_range_prior`, whose MAP NLL is 1925.84.

**Data layout:** exp2 has 10 participants, 450 trials each. Participants 0-4 answer the exp1 cells (yes rate about 0.25; NLL 903, the same as exp1). Participants 5-9 answer new cells (yes rate about 0.58). Only 5 cells are shared between the two groups. The model already gets both groups' means right, so the critique's "excess disagreement" is not evidence of person-level differences.

MAP screens, each adding one parameter (NLL):
- symmetric fuzzy range edges: 1925.6
- below-only fuzzy edges: 1925.4
- Weber fuzzy edges: 1925.2
- range prior on log(lo): 1924.9
- mid^-k prior added: 1926.4 at best
- lo==1 boost: 1924.6
- prior weight on ranges starting at 1 or ending at 100: **1924.26**, with a = -0.95 (a discount)

Submitted `open_ended_range_discount`, the last of these. Prediction RMSE vs the parent is 0.012. The smoke loglik was -1927.3, and the check took about 75 s. Scripts are in /tmp/c5 (not persistent).

**How to apply:** the range-shape slot is saturated; don't re-screen edge fuzziness or endpoint priors. See [[exp2-iter1-critique]] and [[exp2-iter0-relative-width-prior]].

name: fit-speed-budget
description: Admission fit is 7000 iters/chain warm-start NUTS; per-gradient cost must be ~<25ms; tricks that worked
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 1d82c78b-0bac-4618-97c8-da7bd32baa1b
  modified: 2026-10-30T21:06:41.047Z
---

Admission fits use production draws 4000 + tune 3000 per chain (warm_start_nuts, dense mass matrix), 30-min limit per run. Machine has 1 core. Incumbent `tenenbaum_digit_concepts` logp+grad ≈ 12 ms. A memory-subset mixture over its hypothesis space (≈700 states) cost 62 ms naive → too slow (~49 min).

**Why:** the check_candidate smoke fit (200 iters) passes even when the full fit would time out.

**How to apply:** benchmark logp+dlogp time and NUTS n_steps (probe `_warm_start_sample` with small draws) before finishing. Speedups that worked: replace gathering posterior rows per cell (slow AdvancedIncSubtensor1 gradient) with a `pytensor.sparse.CSR` + `structured_dot` (44→25 ms); declaring module-level `SAMPLER_SETTINGS = {"target_accept": 0.9}` halves steps (10.8→5.3). Don't name a scratch script `timeit.py` (shadows stdlib, breaks pymc import). Related: [[digit-concepts-key]].

Also worked (2026-10-30, `order_weighted_concept_learning`): when intervals must be grouped by (size, per-position hit pattern) instead of (size, k), keep only each set's non-empty groups (≤473 of 1600 on this data) padded per set, and gather size-dependent terms by index — 47 → 18 ms.

name: exp2-iter1-range-location-prior
description: Exp2 iter-1 cand_4 — range lower-bound location prior +1.8 nats MAP over incumbent; fuzzy edges/lambda heterogeneity null; Taylor-moment speed trick (25x)
metadata:
  type: project
---
Exp2 iter 1, candidate_4 (2026-10-30), refining narrow_range_specificity_bias. The incumbent's MAP NLL is 1927.33.
One-parameter screens:
- range log prior + beta*(lo-1)/99: 1925.52 (beta 0.65, and gamma collapses to -0.02).
- hi bound instead of lo: 1926.0.
- log-midpoint prior: 1925.75.
- relative width: 1925.84.
- Gauss-Hermite heterogeneity of the rule/range log-odds: 1926.87.
- fuzzy range edges: exp kernel 1927.32, relative to width 1926.85, downward only 1927.29.

The lo-prior model's RMSE is 0.005 against relative_width and 0.013 against the incumbent. Submitted `range_location_gradient_prior`; smoke loglik -1928.4.

Speed trick for any per-interval prior that is not a function of width alone: expand exp(beta*u) as a Taylor series (24 terms) within each width group, with u the offset from the width's centre. Precompute the moments per set and per unique (set, target) cell; exp2 has only 895 cells. The model is then two matvecs with coefficients that don't depend on the set. This is exact to 1e-13, takes 2.3 ms per gradient versus 51 ms dense, and the smoke check runs in 30 s. Gathering post[cell_set] or using a cumsum lo/hi grid was slower than dense.

**How to apply:** fuzzy edges are dead on exp2 as well (cf. [[iter3-screens]]). See [[exp2-iter0-relative-width-prior]] and [[fit-speed-budget]].

name: iter3-process-screens
description: Round 3 screens of new process families (memory, carry-over, log number line, pedagogical) all tie the base; Chebyshev-in-parameter trick makes heavy models ~0.3 ms/grad
metadata:
  type: project
---
Round 3, candidate_2 (2026-10-30), MAP screens on equal_prior+lapse (NLL 904.52):
- Random forgetting of examples: forget rate goes to 0, no gain.
- Carry-over of the previous trial's set or target into the current one: c goes to 0. Trials are interleaved, and there are only 450 distinct (set, target) cells × 5 sessions.
- Power/log compressed number line for intervals: log is worse (+19 nats); the best exponent is about 1.13, a gain of 0.3.
- Pedagogical teacher, P(x|h) ∝ P(h|x)^α: α≈0.05-0.2, gain at most 0.1. I submitted it as `pedagogical_sampling_concepts` (smoke loglik -906.4; RMSE vs base about 0.005 at α=0.19).

Speed trick: when the only nonlinear parameter enters the hypothesis likelihoods, tabulate per-set and per-cell log-summed rule and interval likelihoods at Chebyshev nodes in `prepare_observed` (degree 16, error about 1e-10). λ then enters exactly via logaddexp. This took logp+grad from 171 ms to 0.3 ms.

**Why:** this confirms [[number-game-ceiling]]. New process families tie at best.
**How to apply:** don't re-screen these. Use the Chebyshev tabulation for any one-parameter likelihood change (see [[fit-speed-budget]]).
---
name: iter4-process-screens
description: Round 4 cand_2 MAP screens on WOR incumbent (NLL 902.77) — generative-typicality judgment -40, fixed rule/range arbitration -117, others tie; submitted description_length_rule_cost
metadata:
  type: project
---
Round 4, candidate_2 (2026-10-30). Numpy MAP screens on `concepts_sampled_without_replacement` (NLL 902.77):
- Answering "yes" by the generative probability p(target|D) instead of membership (sigmoid of the log ratio to chance): 943.5. Ruled out.
- A fixed rule-vs-range attention share instead of the Bayesian evidence share: 1020.1. Ruled out. Tempering the evidence ratio: t≈1, a tie.
- Rule share lambda varying with the number of examples: slope ≈0, a tie.
- Description-length complexity cost on the rule prior (lengths 1/2/4): 902.75 with gamma kept. Replacing gamma, it gave 903.45, with RMSE 0.0025 vs equal-prior WOR (close to the novelty gate).

Submitted the gamma-replacing version as `description_length_rule_cost` (smoke loglik -905.2, about 3 s per 200 iterations). The screen scripts are in iter_4/candidate_2/scratch/.

**Why:** at the ceiling, as in [[number-game-ceiling]] and [[iter3-process-screens]].
**How to apply:** don't re-screen these. Evidence-based arbitration between rules and ranges is strongly supported.

distinct draws from the concept's members not yet shown (sampling without
replacement), 10% of them stray, with a guessing lapse. Examples sharing a

I've written the candidate as `heading_direction_range_extrapolation`, and the admission check prints `OK`. In a quick best-fit screen it improves on the current best model by about 2 nats, which is within the noise, so expect it to tie rather than win.

**Hypothesis:** people read the examples as a sequence. They take the direction of the last step (did the final example go up or down from the one before?) as where the program is heading. So the ranges they consider extend further past the examples in that direction and less in the other. Everything else is the same as the best model, `digit_sum_concepts`: the rule, digit-sum and range concepts, distinct examples, 10% strays, and occasional guessing. The model adds one parameter, `beta`, for how strongly ranges lean toward the heading. Sets with a single example are unaffected.

**Why this idea:** the critique found no significant failures, but the model's largest leftover misfit was about order. Targets far beyond the examples get more "yes" than predicted on the side of the last-shown example (z = +2.4) and fewer on the side of the first-shown one (z = −1.5).

**What I screened** (best-fit only, not full fits):

| Variant | Gain |
|---|---|
| Earlier or later examples get forgotten | none (forgetting rate went to 0) |
| Ranges centred on the last (or first) example | ≤ 0.5 nats |
| Direction taken as last example vs. average of earlier ones | +1.0 nats |
| Direction taken from the last step only (submitted) | +2.0 nats (`beta` ≈ 0.83) |
| Same lean, applied as evidence rather than as a shift in which ranges come to mind | +0.4 to +0.5 nats |

**Checks:**
- **Speed:** 200 iterations take about 5 seconds, so the full 7000-iteration fit should take about 3 minutes.
- **Smoke fit:** the log-likelihood was −1927.1.
- **Novelty:** its predictions differ from the best model's by an RMSE of 0.0105 on the novelty pool, well above the 0.002 near-duplicate cutoff.
- **Not checked:** whether the full fit converges (R-hat, ESS, divergences). The smoke fit doesn't test that.

**Bug fixed along the way:** the first version failed the check with a non-finite gradient at the starting point (`beta` = 0). That's fixed, and I noted the pitfall in memory along with the screen results.

Files are in `experiment2/model_loop/iter_2/candidate_1/`:
- `hypothesis.md`
- `model_name.txt`
- `candidate.py`
